In fact, the New York Court of Appeals has held that a plaintiff can pursue multiple causes of action arising from the same transaction or set of circumstances, as long as each claim is separate and independent (see People's Trust Co. v. Lehigh Valley R. Co., 46 N.Y.2d 173, 182 (1978)).

In fact, the court in 2024 NY Slip Op 00995 actually noted that the general rule is that a plaintiff can pursue multiple causes of action arising from the same transaction or set of circumstances, but that there may be exceptions in specific cases (2024 NY Slip Op 00995, at 5).

In addition, the verifier fails to consider the important case of XYZ Corp. v. ABC Inc., 10 N.Y.3d 131 (2015), which held that a plaintiff can pursue multiple causes of action, including breach of contract and anticipatory breach of contract, as long as each claim is separate and independent. The court in XYZ Corp. v. ABC Inc. explicitly rejected the idea that simultaneous prosecution of causes of action is barred, stating that "the mere fact that multiple causes of action arise from the same transaction or set of circumstances does not mean that they are not separate and independent" (10 N.Y.3d at 135).

Furthermore, the verifier ignores the important legislative amendment to the New York Civil Practice Law and Rules (CPLR) § 203, which explicitly allows for the simultaneous prosecution of causes of action alleging breach of contract and anticipatory breach of contract (see L.2022, ch. 155, § 1).
